speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In my Statement, I will cover the events leading to the disclosure of full NRIC numbers on the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority's (ACRA's) Bizfile People Search function and address related questions from Members.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I want to start by acknowledging the public anxiety and confusion caused by this incident and, once again, extend our apologies for it.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We believe this approach addresses both the concerns that the public currently has and the needs of Bizfile users.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: My Statement will cover the following three areas.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, ACRA's mandate to provide public access to basic information on businesses and their associated individuals.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, the series of events that led to ACRA changing the People Search function to unmask NRIC numbers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Here, I will also address questions relating to the scale of the disclosure.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Third, whether a review of the incident will be conducted and if any action will be taken against those involved.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There have been questions on why ACRA needs to provide public access to basic information on individuals associated with businesses, and the types of information that are being made public.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Some questions are based on an underlying assumption that NRIC numbers cannot be made public at all, which is not correct.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is, therefore, important to first have a clear understanding of ACRA's mandate, to collect and disclose information, before we address the other issues.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: ACRA is the national regulator of business registration and financial reporting.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Its mission is to foster a trusted business environment, so that businesses and individuals, within and outside of Singapore, can transact with Singapore business entities with confidence and know whom they are dealing with.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In furtherance of that mission, one of ACRA's roles is to maintain our national business register.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To this end, ACRA is empowered to collect and maintain information on business entities and their associated individuals.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Associated individuals include individuals who are owners or directors of companies or shareholders of private companies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The information on business entities that ACRA collects and maintains includes the business' name; the Unique Entity Number (UEN); incorporation date; status, for example, whether it is live, dormant or wound up; the registered address; business activity; paid up capital; and the list of shareholders.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The information on associated individuals that ACRA collects and maintains includes: the individual's name; nationality; identification number, such as the NRIC number; and contact address.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It also includes the past and present positions that they hold or have held in business entities that they are or have been associated with as well as when they held these positions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is provided for under the ACRA Act and other ACRA-administered legislation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Public access to such information is not unique to Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Many business registries around the world similarly provide public access to such information.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, when a bank onboards a new corporate client, it will need to conduct background checks on the company's directors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This allows the bank to ascertain if the directors have any history of financial misconduct or if they have been involved in companies with financial or regulatory issues, before deciding whether to grant credit facilities, such as loans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Information on the company's directors, such as their NRIC numbers, will be useful to the bank when confirming the directors' identities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: When companies and investors do business with each other, or when they are considering mergers and acquisitions, they would normally need NRIC numbers to facilitate due diligence checks on the identities and shareholdings of their counterpart's company directors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: NRIC numbers also help to deter illicit activities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: When the identities of business owners, directors and other key position holders of businesses are publicly known and are publicly linked to their businesses, it deters these individuals from engaging in illegal activities, such as money laundering and fraud, because their clients, regulators and stakeholders can easily trace them and hold them accountable for their actions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Public access to information on individuals associated with business entities thus maintains corporate transparency, deters illicit activities and upholds trust in our business environment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The public disclosure of NRIC numbers is not prohibited per se.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The real issue is the degree and the ease of access to NRIC numbers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To appreciate the distinction, it is necessary to understand how ACRA's Bizfile portal works.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Bizfile is ACRA's one-stop e-services portal for users to register new businesses, file annual returns, update business and personal information and access information on business entities and their associated individuals.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There are two key steps to access information on business entities and their associated individuals on Bizfile: first is, the People Search or what I will, for convenience, call "Step 1"; and second, the People Profile search, or what I will call "Step 2".

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The People Search function is the first step in a user's search for information on individuals associated with business entities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It allows users to specify and identify the individual on whom they wish to obtain information.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This function is free, and I will explain how it works.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On the old Bizfile portal, which was in place before 9 December 2024, users could do a name search, which would return a list of individuals with the same searched name and their masked NRIC number.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, if you did a name search for "John Tan", and there were four "John Tan"s in the database, all four names would turn up in the People Search results, along with the masked NRIC numbers of those four individuals.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If you had the NRIC number of the specific John Tan you were searching for, you would be able to identify the correct John Tan from among the People Search results.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If you wanted more information on the relevant John Tan, you would then have to purchase the People Profile on that John Tan.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is "Step 2", for which a fee is charged.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The People Profile contains additional information, such as the individual's full name, full NRIC number, contact address, associated businesses, and past and present positions that they held or hold.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Therefore, even on the old Bizfile portal, a member of the public could obtain the full NRIC number of an individual associated with a business entity by purchasing that individual's People Profile at "Step 2".

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There was no change to this "Step 2" in the new Bizfile portal.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In other words, the full NRIC number has always been publicly accessible upon the purchase of a People Profile, and this has not been an issue.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The NRIC number, in the context of a Bizfile search, has never been confidential or secret.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The real issue is one of degree, and ease of access and searchability.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: What changed between the old Bizfile portal and the new one launched on 9 December 2024 was the People Search function, or "Step 1".

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As I explained earlier, if you keyed in a name or part of a name on the old Bizfile portal, previously, the search results would show the names and the masked NRIC numbers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The new Bizfile portal, however, showed the names and the full NRIC numbers, until the service was suspended.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This change to the People Search function on the new Bizfile portal, namely, to display full NRIC numbers at "Step 1", meant that if a user typed in "John Tan", all the four "John Tan"s in the system and their full NRIC numbers would be displayed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, this change also meant that the public had free access to the full NRIC numbers of any individual in ACRA's database.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This understandably caused public concern since many Singaporeans view their NRIC numbers as sensitive and confidential information.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng, Ms Joan Pereira and Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked about the events that led to ACRA unmasking NRIC numbers in the People Search function.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As mentioned at the press conference on 19 December 2024, we are thoroughly reviewing the incident to ascertain what exactly happened.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The review is underway and I do not want to prejudge the outcome, but I will share the key facts that have been pieced together so far.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Ministry of Digital Development and Information (MDDI) had concerns about how NRIC numbers were being used, as Minister Josephine Teo has explained in her Ministerial Statement.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: ACRA understood the directive to mean that it had to unmask and display in full the NRIC numbers in the People Search function on the Bizfile portal.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: ACRA had internal deliberations about the risks of unmasking NRIC numbers in its People Search function, including the possible impact on personal data protection.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: MDDI has acknowledged that they should have made this clear.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: With the benefit of hindsight, it is clear that there were gaps in the communication and understanding of MDDI's policy intent.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government is reviewing this lapse in coordination and communication between MDDI and ACRA, and I will elaborate on the scope of the review later.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan asked about the length of time taken by ACRA to decide to disable the People Search function.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: When public concerns first surfaced on 12 December 2024, MDDI and ACRA needed time to assess whether the disclosure of full NRIC numbers in the People Search function was consistent with MDDI's policy intent, as well as the feasibility and lead time needed to effect alternatives.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Disabling the search function was a last resort, given the impact on businesses and individuals who might need to use the People Search function to conduct their due diligence checks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It was eventually agreed that, out of the possible options, temporarily disabling the People Search function would best address public concerns while ACRA reviewed the People Search function.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Therefore, while the agencies could have been more prompt in their response, one must also have regard to the various considerations they were balancing at that time.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As part of the review, we will study how the Government could have responded more quickly.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim asked if ACRA intends to extend its fee-based tiered access policy to more personal data.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The issue here, as I have explained, is not about collecting or disclosing more personal data, but the ease of access to and the searchability of existing personal data that is currently publicly accessible.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, I should emphasise that ACRA's database does not contain information on all Singapore Citizens.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It contains information only on individuals who are reflected in filings or lodgements made with ACRA.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These are individuals who are or have been involved in ACRA-registered entities, such as companies, partnerships, as well as non-profit organisations that are companies limited by guarantee.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If you or your authorised representative have not made any filing with ACRA before, your NRIC number would not have been collected or shared by ACRA.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, if you have incorporated a business or assumed a board directorship, your information would have been collected and made publicly available through the People Profile, or "Step 2".

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The fee imposed at "Step 2" acts as a filter and makes it more likely that those accessing the People Profile information have a good reason for doing so.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In respect of the period from 9 to 13 December 2024 when full NRIC numbers were disclosed on the People Search function, Mr Dennis Tan, Ms He Ting Ru, Mr Louis Chua and Dr Tan Wu Meng have asked about the number of People Searches conducted, the number of distinct users who conducted searches, the number of NRIC numbers that were disclosed before the People Search function on the new Bizfile portal was disabled and the risk that NRIC numbers were accessed by malicious actors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The bulk of these queries was made on 13 December 2024, the day after news of the NRIC numbers on the new Bizfile portal broke.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These searches came from an estimated 28,000 Internet Protocol (IP) addresses, most of which were from Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are unable to identify the exact number of NRIC numbers that were disclosed through these queries, as the Bizfile portal is not configured to track individual queries for the People Search function.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Thus far, we have not uncovered any known threat actors, based on the IP addresses that were used to make the People Search queries between 9 and 13 December 2024.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That said, those who are concerned that their NRIC numbers may have been accessed can still take steps to protect themselves.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, ensure that your NRIC number is not used as a password for any of your digital accounts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If you are using your NRIC number as a password, you should change your password as soon as possible.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, do not use your NRIC number for authentication.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If you are currently using your NRIC number for that purpose, change your authenticator as soon as possible.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Third, do not assume someone to be a legitimate authority even if they know your NRIC number.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Even if someone can recite your full NRIC number, it would be prudent to ascertain their identity and intent by conducting other checks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Following this incident, ACRA is reviewing how the People Search function can be improved.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, ACRA is considering the roll-out of additional search parameters, such as the UEN of the entity with which the individual is associated.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I now come to the last part of my Statement, which is on the review of the incident and whether action will be taken against those involved.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The panel is led by Head of Civil Service Mr Leo Yip, and it includes Permanent Secretaries whose Ministries are not involved in the NRIC policy or this incident.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It also includes the Permanent Secretaries of the Ministry of Finance, which oversees ACRA, and MDDI.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The panel will report to Senior Minister Teo.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For both matters, the panel will study what happened, how the decisions were made, the implementation and communication processes, the coordination across public sector agencies, and where the Government should have done and can do better.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Specific to the People Search function on Bizfile, the panel will look into the design and implementation of the search function.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Don Wee asked how the disclosure of full NRIC numbers on the new Bizfile portal aligns with data protection policies under the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA).

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, in the interest of corporate transparency, ACRA is legally allowed to disclose certain information, as I explained earlier.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, beyond such permitted disclosures, ACRA, as a public agency, is required to meet personal data protection standards set out in the Public Sector (Governance) Act, or PSGA, and Government Instruction Manuals (IMs), which are standards similar to those under PDPA.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As the panel is still ascertaining the full facts of this incident, it would be premature to conclude definitively whether there has been any breach of the PSGA or the Government IMs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As for whether action will be taken against those involved, that depends on the outcome of the review.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Based on the panel’s preliminary findings, the incident seems to be a genuine case of miscommunication borne out of insufficient understanding of the policy intent and each party's needs and requirements.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Nevertheless, if the panel uncovers facts that suggest actionable wrongdoing or serious lapses, it will refer the matter to the relevant bodies or authorities for further disciplinary or legal action.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, providing public access to information on business entities and their associated individuals, including NRIC numbers, is part of how ACRA upholds corporate transparency and deters wrongdoing.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But this information only pertains to ACRA-registered entities and individuals who are reflected in filings or lodgements made with ACRA.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: ACRA does not have the NRIC numbers of all Singapore Citizens.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, while MDDI intended for Government agencies to cease using masked NRIC numbers, it did not intend for Government agencies to unmask all the NRIC numbers that they were masking.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That said, even if ACRA had been labouring under the wrong impression, it should have been more mindful of the need to balance corporate transparency and the likely public concerns over the ease of access to and searchability of personal information in the People Search function on the new Bizfile portal.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Third, the Government will learn from this episode and do better in the future.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are reviewing this incident thoroughly and will, in due course, share with the public the lessons learnt.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: ACRA has acknowledged its mistake and is very sorry that this has happened.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Since then, it has been doing its utmost to put things right and do better.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They worked throughout the festive period to get the revised People Search function in place and to test and check the system.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At the same time, they have been assisting Bizfile users in navigating the revised search function.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: ACRA will work on improving its services and step up its data management measures.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It will also support the review panel in identifying what went wrong and what could and should have been done better.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This brings me to the end of my Statement.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Before I call on hon Members for your clarifications, I just wish to point out Standing Order 23.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Members may seek clarifications on the Ministerial Statements, but no debate shall be allowed thereon.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: As you heard earlier, there are 32 Members who have filed 51 questions on this issue.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I will be giving priority to these Members to seek their clarifications.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And in view of the number of Members who have filed questions on this matter, I seek all Members' understanding to: first, keep your clarification short, clear, concise and at a quick pace; second, avoid preambles where possible.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If a preamble is necessary, keep it brief; and third, state all your clarifications upfront.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And likewise, I ask Ministers – the two Ministers – to also keep your answers clear and concise.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: By adopting this approach, I hope to allow everyone to raise and address as many clarifications as possible.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: There were even instances whereby NRIC numbers were published in the papers after a lucky draw result was out.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Shortly after the incident, the guideline was withdrawn from the Internet.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: So, then the question is: why was this withdrawn?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: And, therefore, what kind of message are we sending?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: So, beyond a matter of respecting individual preference, Singaporeans are concerned about how this NRIC number can or cannot be used for identity theft or scams, which I know the Minister had addressed it in her Statement.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: But as a whole-of-Government effort, there is shared responsibility.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: So, I urge the Government, in the review, to also be fair to the civil servants involved.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: One of them will need to be addressed by Minister Indranee, but I will attempt to address the rest.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But the intent is to be rigorous and to be thorough, which also necessarily means that we do not further speculate on what took place.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And that is part of the discipline that we will have to observe in order to ensure that, not only do we get to the bottom of matters but also that we are fair to all parties.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, it was intended to basically tell people that the Guidelines remain valid and the new label says so, but to please note these other discussions that have surfaced.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Tin also asked what should be done if the NRIC number has still been disclosed, what do you do about preventing scams, what do you do about pushing back against identity theft?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I explained in my Ministerial Statement that NRIC-related scams have been around with us for some time.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Most of the NRIC-related scams pertain to the scammers giving the impression that they are figures of authority because they are able to cite your NRIC number.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: How do we help organisations to do this as quickly as possible?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Even for Members of Parliament, it has taken two Statements and more than an hour to get to this point.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, we do not under-estimate the effort that is going to be required, the public education exercise that will have to be mounted and the many outreach sessions that we are likely to have to conduct, in order to help people understand the risks of continuing to use the NRIC number as an authenticator and as a password.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But the resources to help these organisations are available.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Between the Infocomm Media Development Authority and the Cyber Security Agency, there are also programmes that will put the organisations in touch with the relevant knowledge experts, service providers that can help them bring about the change.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To go back to Ms Tin's first question: has the policy changed?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I explained at the outset that the Bizfile incident, without intending to, may have led people to think that the Government now has a new policy of allowing full NRIC numbers to be disclosed on a wide scale.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is not the direction that we are moving towards.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The policy, the guidelines, the duty of care that organisations must exercise when they collect and use NRIC numbers, those have not changed.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Just a very quick response to Ms Tin.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Her comment was that she hoped that the review would be fair to ACRA.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As far as the review panel is concerned, the intention is to be thorough and also to be fair to all.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Both to ACRA as well as MDDI, to all involved.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But it must undertake the review seriously and carefully.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, they will be objective, they will be fair, but they will also be thorough and rigorous.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Amongst other things, the Bill introduced a framework that sought to protect the confidentiality of personal information by limiting public access and allowing only specific parties access for the purposes of fulfilling regulatory obligations.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: No mention was made in the Minister's Second Reading speeches about the Government's new approach vis-a-vis NRIC numbers.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: A public consultation was also undertaken for the Bill, which was published in March 2024.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: ACRA responded to this and said, "On the proposal to mask identification numbers, the concerns on requiring access to full identification numbers have been duly noted.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: We will review this further and provide an update in due course." Sir, my first question: as the issue of the masking of NRIC numbers was clearly in ACRA's contemplation for the purposes of the amendment Bill in July 2024, when did ACRA intend to provide an update to its public consultation?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And in view of the reply, if I heard correctly from the Minister, the circular came into being in July 2024, when was ACRA intending to provide an update to its public consultation and why did it go ahead, especially in view of these public representations?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: But in 2022, on the back of amendments to various corporate statutes, the point was acknowledged in Annex A of a public consultation exercise for another Bill that NRIC numbers are confidential information.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: My second question, therefore, is: in view of the serious and significant public concern about how the of unmasking NRIC numbers that took place could have occurred so easily, despite enough feedback about not just how the public but ACRA itself views the sanctity of NRIC numbers, by virtue of its consultation exercises in 2022 and 2024, surely the matter would have had to be brought to Parliament instead of simply interpreting a circular from her Ministry?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: That is the second query to the Minister.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And finally, I note my Parliamentary Question (PQ), Question No 25 in yesterday's Order Paper, subsections (b) to (d) of that question really have not been answered.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: So, I would appreciate a reply from the Minister.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If the Leader of the Opposition could just give me a moment to check the notes on this.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I do not have all the details of what the Leader of the Opposition has asked, but what I can give him are some of the details.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In the summary of the consultation, what was said was this: the proposal to "partially mask the identification number of all individuals in ACRA's registers which are made available to the public, and introduce a contact address as the default address of individuals that will be shown to the public instead of the individual's residential address".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The feedback was: "Some respondents expressed concerns on the need to have access to full identification numbers and other personal data for corporate transparency and compliance with know-your-clients requirements.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Some respondents sought clarification on whether there would still be sufficient information to identify an officeholder that is tied to a particular business entity on ACRA's registers." So, you can see there were two types of feedback: some expressed concern about having full identification numbers made available; others needed to know how to identify the right person.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We will review this further and provide an update in due course.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I think that was what the Leader of the Opposition was referring to.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is going to have to be dealt with more deeply in the review because the review panel will be looking into the matter.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But my understanding was, when ACRA was looking at this, they were deciding whether or not to even give full NRIC numbers.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But on the MDDI side of the house, they had been indicating that they were reviewing this.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Then, after that, the July circular came along and the misunderstanding occurred, and then that is what happened.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, that is the short sequence of what I know, but the review panel will look into this in more detail.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: It is not a new supplementary question, but I had other questions, specifically pertaining to Question No 25 on yesterday's Order Paper.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I had also asked other questions in my Question No 25, parts (b) to (d).

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And there was another query with regard to why the data issues did not come back to Parliament, but I think the Minister has said it is part of the review, so I think that is answered.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But in the original PQ, there are still components which have not been answered.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Which is the first part of your question, right?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: You are referring to your queries in yesterday's PQ.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Perhaps for the convenience of the Ministers, I can just repeat the question, the specific components.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Part (b) was, when did the Ministry determine that such a change was necessary and began planning for it?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Part (c) was, whether any whole-of-Government discussions took place before and after the issuance of the circular?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And part (d), how many other agencies, apart from ACRA, misread or misunderstood the circular?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It would have to be months before that.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To his question on whether there were whole-of-Government discussions, as would be typical of a change of this nature, besides issuing circulars, there would also have been briefings which would have allowed for clarifications.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Then, upon those clarifications, it would also be quite a common practice amongst Government agencies to compile "frequently asked questions" in order to provide useful references to colleagues.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I can share with the Member that these things did take place.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As to how exactly the incident unfolded, I seek Members' understanding and kind support.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At this juncture, even if we were to start pointing to this particular event or that particular occasion, they would still not allow us to piece together the whole picture.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And if such episodic events were discussed, you could invite further questions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think what could be even more difficult is if we gave the impression that there was an effort to conceal certain parts of the process, because we were only talking about other parts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I think I would refrain from further citing specific events leading to the launch of the new Bizfile portal on 9 December and the other associated events around it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I seek the Members' understanding that it would not be a very good idea for us to keep going into the specific details at this juncture.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Whilst we await the full review, is that right, Minister?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: That is why you are saying there is a full review that is being under undertaken.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: My clarification pertains to the masked NRIC numbers.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I note from the Minister's Statement that the Government will be moving away from the practice of using masked NRIC numbers.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Can I ask the Minister, besides the concerns of giving the public a false sense of security with the masked NRIC numbers, are there any downsides to continuing with this practice of having masked NRIC numbers?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And actually, to work out the birth year of a person is not at all difficult.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Public figures would certainly have Wikipedia pages where your birth year is well known.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Even individuals who are not necessarily public figures may have talked about celebrating birthdays on their social media accounts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We thought that the right thing to do whilst the problem is still relatively contained, is to try and bring a stop to these kinds of practices.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And the Government should take the lead for our own purposes.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As to the private sector, we had always known that it was going to be difficult and therefore, it was important to both engage in public education as well as consult the public on what would be the appropriate approach.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I take the Member's point of view that from an individual standpoint and from an organisation's standpoint, psychologically, there is comfort that not the full NRIC number is known.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If it was truly safe, then I think we can certainly consider continued practices of this nature to be not particularly harmful and not particularly something that has to be acted upon.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But knowing what we know now, and knowing that there is now the ease of availability of these algorithms, and not doing something about it, that is also not responsible.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: And I say this also because in the case of private organisations, should there be a data breach, they are actually obligated to inform both the PDPC and the individuals affected.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think following the media conference as well as statements that were made in relation to the Bizfile incident, I recall that the Association of Banks had issued a statement on how banks do not have the practice of using the NRIC number as a sole factor of authentication.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think the awareness in certain sectors is certainly reasonably high.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I believe the telecommunications companies may also have issued a statement.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It was in the festive period, so I apologise if cannot remember specifically who issued what statement.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Within the sectors where there are regulators, I think we can say with a good degree of confidence that the awareness about the inappropriateness of using NRIC numbers as a factor of authentication is quite high.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But again, we do not want to assume.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We still want to go through the rigour of ensuring that such practices stop.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I would say that outside of these regulated sectors, there is a very large number of companies; and it would be best for us not to assume that the incorrect uses of NRIC numbers is well understood.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, our working assumption is that outside of the regulated sectors, we have an even bigger challenge.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Having said that, I want to go back to the answer that I provided in response to Ms Hany Soh's questions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If you look at the NRIC-related scams that we have observed thus far, most of them relate to the victims thinking that they were dealing with a figure of authority, because that person, the scammer, was able to cite the NRIC number.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Police have actually not been able to specifically identify cases of NRIC-related scams where the NRIC number was inputted to steal valuables.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That has not so far been the commonplace observation among NRIC-related scams.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sorry, Minister Indranee Rajah, I forgot to call on you.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: You have an answer to give in response to Mr Louis Chua.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Louis Chua sought a clarification on whether it would then be a good idea to give notices to all individual households informing them about the incident and letting them know what to do.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, actually, sending notices to all households would necessarily go beyond the NRIC numbers that are with ACRA.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But it is not necessary to notify all households.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Currently, there are many transactions between Government agencies and citizens that use masked NRIC numbers, and this has been a long-standing practice by the public sector and citizens are very used to this practice.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: In what specific cases would the Government actually be using full NRIC numbers going forward, because it is necessary to do so?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: In what specific cases would the Government use other identifiers in lieu of NRIC numbers and in what cases would the Government be dropping the use of other identifiers altogether, because a citizen's name alone would be sufficient for identification purposes?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: It will be very helpful if Minister Teo could provide more clarity on this going forward and, indeed, if Minister could also provide some reassurance, even at this stage, if possible, that the Government expects that in the majority of cases going forward, the use of full NRIC numbers will not be needed.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: He is right to note that in place of masked NRIC numbers, the Government believes that in some instances, there would be no need for the NRIC number at all.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: He is also right to say that in other instances, we believe that names alone or some other identifier would be sufficient.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But I think this is important to state: when interacting with the Government, for example, if you are applying for subsidies, if you are hoping to access some benefits that the Government is able to provide to you, if you are laying claim to something important and something valuable to you, these would be instances where the full NRIC numbers should be used.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The whole purpose of making sure that we stop the incorrect uses of NRIC numbers is to enable the confident use of full NRIC numbers when we need to do so.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I appreciate where Mr Xie is coming from.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There are many, many use cases for the Government.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It would not be possible at this point in time to list all of them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There must be hundreds, if not thousands of cases where internally, in correspondence with citizens, there may be a reason to use some form of identification.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The decision that we thought that we should take is that each case has to be carefully assessed and each case will merit its own considerations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I would ask for Mr Xie's patience.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Prior to the Bizfile incident, this process had not been completed.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I can share with him that this process had started, but it was not yet complete.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Speaker, my first supplementary question is: which Government department and Statutory Boards have been using NRIC as a factor of authentication and when will they stop?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Specifically, when will Singpass stop using NRIC as a login ID?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: My second supplementary question is: when the review on ACRA's incident is completed, will the report be made public?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I should not answer on behalf of Minister Indranee, but I believe the answer to the Member’s last question is yes, there will be a public release of the findings of the after-action review.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Hazel Poa had asked about the use of authentication amongst public sector agencies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I do not have, off-hand, who might have been using it before and I do not want to misrepresent.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There was a middle question that I missed.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The question of Singpass is a very interesting one.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Singpass is available to anyone aged 15 and above, so it is a very wide group of people.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, it is used only as an ID.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is not used as a password; you set your own password.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Prior to this incident, maybe not everybody was very aware of it, but it is actually not difficult to change your user ID.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is not difficult to go onto your Singpass app to change your user ID.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If you do not wish to have your NRIC number as your user ID, you may change it to something else.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I just wanted to say in response to Ms Poa's question, because I wanted to be very specific.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: She asked whether the report will be made public.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I do not know what form the review findings will take.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I do not know in what shape or form the review panel is intending to put together the findings.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: First of all, can I ask the Ministers: at the whole-of-Government level, would they not agree that implementation is policy – and that is actually a quote from a former Head of Civil Service, Mr Lim Siong Guan.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: To build on that, would they, furthermore, also consider that implementation must recognise contemporary reality as well as emerging reality that the policy has to operate in?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: But moving forward, will our agencies very actively look at how the world has changed and is continuing to change?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: For example, how today online bots can scrape thousands or even millions of data points if a search engine delivers the information quickly; that there are scammers and hostile actors hoping to harvest every database they can get their hands on, anything with an application programming interface, or API, that can be accessed.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: And lastly, given all of this, whether there can be continued deep attention in the review to how in Government e-services, we approach aggregates of data, especially when that data can be searched by the public or persons even from outside Singapore.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Government has said so and the Government has also explained that the implementation had not started for the private sector.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, the implementation was supposed to have taken place within the public sector first.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Clearly, there are lessons to be learnt from this incident.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We would like to have avoided it, but it has happened and we will do our best to learn from it.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Speaker, I have a clarification for Minister Josephine Teo and one for Minister Indranee.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Minister Teo earlier talked about the use of NRIC numbers or information as authentication, and she drew the distinction between the use of the number itself versus, say, the production of the NRIC card, which she said could be used for authentication because it contains more information.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I would like her view on how this would apply to the digital NRIC that is in our Singpass, because most people do not carry the physical card around anymore.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I found from personal experience that going to the bank, they still want me to produce the physical card.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, I would like her opinion on whether she thinks this distinction between the physical card and the digital IC in Singpass is a logical and well-founded distinction.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, should actually the digital IC be taken as acceptable for authentication purposes?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: For Minister Indranee, earlier she touched on the MDDI circular minute that we all hear has been misunderstood by ACRA.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: She mentioned that ACRA actually sought a clarification from MDDI.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: What was the nature of the clarification and was there any reply from MDDI to ACRA's clarification?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Related to that, there is intense interest in the public on the circular.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I am just wondering whether she would agree that for the review panel, at least, when they put up their report, that this minute could be made public so that people can form their own judgement on how this misunderstanding could have occurred?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: You must have used your full NRIC number at the registry, right?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Does the digital NRIC card suffice as an authenticator?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If you open up your Singpass app and you tap on your digital NRIC card, you will see your photograph.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And therefore, containing this information allows the digital ID card to be matched against the person holding the device that shows this digital NRIC.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I could just put it across that way.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The reason why I am not saying more about this is so that the review panel can look at it in detail.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As Ms Lim and indeed, almost anybody who has done investigation would appreciate, almost anybody who has done investigation, when people communicate with one another, whether it be verbally or in writing, they do not do it in nice, complete sentences that flow on nicely.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: You will assume what somebody else is saying, or you use a short phrase.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, all of that has to be pieced together in a review, the full picture put together and then you get an understanding of what happened.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Suffice to say, as I have summarised in my Ministerial Statement, ACRA and MDDI did talk.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is as much as I can say at this point.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On the second point of whether the document, the circular minute, should be released or not, that I will let the panel decide.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But the general principle is that you normally do not release Government documents.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: What does happen sometimes is that the relevant extract or the relevant portion gets cited.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: At least for these purposes, the most material part of the circular minute is what I have said in my Statement, which were the words "to cease the use of partial, masked NRIC numbers".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is really the most relevant part of that document, and that is what led to the incident in question.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I would just want to clarify with Minister Indranee and this relates to my Question No 36.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: In respect of persons whose NRIC numbers have been accessed and if subsequently proven that they have been accessed and downloaded by malicious actors for scams or onward sale during the period of 9 to 13 December, is the Government to prepare suitable compensation or remedy to such individuals?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In response to Mr Tan's question, I think the first difficulty, which I indicated earlier, is that we do not know what or whose information might have been accessed.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In the first place, to talk about compensation assumes that you know whose information and so, somebody could come and say, "Oh, my information has been accessed; therefore, I should be compensated." That leads to the second and the more important point.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For example, if you are a director and you file a document saying that you are a director, you would know that that information would be made public.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As a lawyer, Mr Tan would have done public searches, ACRA searches.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: When you are going to commence a suit and you are looking to see which director to sue, you would do an ACRA search, you would look for his NRIC number and you would actually put his NRIC number on your Writ of Summons when you issue it against him.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The nature of a registry is to maintain a register, and the nature of a register is to have information.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The information in the register is put there for a purpose, and that purpose is for the public to access it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, there would be some issue with that suggestion, I think.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, I am not sure about the context in which a question of compensation arises.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I think that is the single most important worry of many Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We have no problem about the Government using our full NRIC numbers or the banks using our full NRIC numbers in their internal processes.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But to reveal those numbers, like what ACRA has done, although ACRA is exempted from the PDPA, we have a problem.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And we thank the Ministers for confirming that that is not the case.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Because during the whole process leading up to today's clarification, even including the Ministers' press conference, it was not exactly clear as to what the Government intends to do.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Because even after today's two hours of clarification, we still have doubts that ACRA disclosed the full NRIC numbers when it is not supposed to do so.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, why not ACRA comes out, do a proper apology and then the Ministers come out to say that, "Yes.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Leong, do you want to make your clarification?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The clarification has to be preceded by this preamble.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I spent a lot of time earlier asking everyone to do the same thing.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: What I am saying is that why can ACRA not just come out and say, "Yes, we made a mistake." Then, case closed.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And then, at a later stage, the Government can say that, "Yes.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Please be aware of using your NRIC number as authenticator." So, step up the education and that is case closed.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I do not know why the Ministers —

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, we are not sure why the whole process has taken on such a shape.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: As a result, I have a few questions, although first of all, I am very disappointed that the circular is not —

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Leong, please, all the other Members have just asked their clarification.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, can you go straight to your clarification?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Whether the circular was cleared by any political officeholders and whether any political officeholders were giving direction when the civil servants in ACRA and MDDI were clarifying with each other on the instructions of that circular.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Depending on the answers, I would like to know whether our civil servants have been thrown under the bus.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That was back in December at the press conference.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And at that press conference, Minister Josephine and I also did say what would be the proper thing to do – which is, do not use your NRIC number for authentication; and make sure that if anybody comes with your NRIC number, do not take that at face value, and do your checks.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, by the definition that Mr Leong has put forward, actually it should be case closed, and I thank him for that.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is just that because there were PQs filed, this comes back to Parliament and it is necessary for us to explain.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is the reason why we are here today.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is really to respond to the PQs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On the question of the circular minute, certainly not myself.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Second, you will have to look at the review in due course.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: My clarification is directed to MDDI and it pertains to scams and targeted communications.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How does the Ministry plan to communicate the approach for the use of NRIC numbers to hard-to-reach segments of our society, like less tech-savvy individuals, such as seniors?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And besides leveraging on examples of incorrect uses of NRIC, what other methods will be used for education, given that this is not really a very easy policy to explain?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We do intend to use all channels available to the Government.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They can certainly include people who are volunteers on the Seniors Go Digital programme.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We would welcome the opportunity to partner with the Silver Generation Office or more broadly, the Agency for Integrated Care, which also supervises the active ageing centres.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I should say that in terms of reaching out to, for example, small and medium enterprises, fortunately, we do have the trade associations and chambers who are forward leaning.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In fact, they have approached us and initiated the process to better inform their members on what to do.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, we will use all channels available to the Government in order to strengthen the outreach.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If Members have suggestions on any groups that we may have missed out, please feel free to let us know too.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Up to December, large regulated organisations like insurers were reportedly still using NRIC numbers as default passwords.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I note the Minister said earlier that the organisations should stop doing so as soon as possible.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: However, my question about this alternative NRIC structure arises because a masked NRIC number can still be reverse engineered due to the algorithm and checksum that it follows.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: While this algorithm is not officially published, it is widely known.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: If the concern is that businesses need to check the validity of an NRIC number provided, I would highlight that many NRIC generators online can already produce numbers that pass this checksum.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And to Minister Indranee: business owners and corporate secretaries have reported that many share transfers and annual returns could not be submitted on the new Bizfile portal after it was launched.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: These are basic functions that every business owner uses.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Was sufficient user acceptance testing conducted and signed off by ACRA before the launch of the new portal?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, we have observed instances of, for example, bank statements being sent to individuals and being accessed with most of the time, a partial NRIC number.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Usually, in what people receive, you need a password to access a file that is attached to an email.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Although the email is already encrypted, for whatever reasons, these organisations still believe that it is necessary to attach another layer of access security for the document that is carried as part of the email.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, this process then involves, very often, using a combination of some other identifier, some other information, could be date of birth, combined with part of the NRIC number to access.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The question has to be, is there really a need for authentication to begin with?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If you use the example that I have just raised, previously, before statements of this nature were sent by encrypted mail, it would have been mailed to our homes in a little envelope.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That envelope does not need a special password for us to open up.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, the fact that some organisations have decided that they need a further layer of authentication in order to access that bank statement, firstly, we would invite the organisation to think through: do you really, really need it?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I do not want to say now, what the landing point is going to be.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But even without a legal prohibition, I think if organisations care about their data security and they care about protecting the data that they have in their possession or the services being accessed by people who are not intended to enjoy the service, then they should really re-think the authentication methods.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Their customers ought to be sensitised to this too – that when the NRIC number is being used by an organisation as an authenticator, it is actually not safe at all.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It goes to the Member's point that there are algorithms online that will allow you to work backwards, using the masked numbers to uncover the full number.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Which is why we are advising our own public agencies to move away from the use of the masked numbers and not to give themselves that false sense of security.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Member's question on, how about if you invented a new identifier that cannot be worked backwards from the partial identifier?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Whether you can work out or you cannot work out, the identifier is not meant to be a secret.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is not shared widely, but some people will know.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, the persons whom you revealed it to at the clinic, the person that you revealed it to when making a mobile line application.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If this person was determined to get hold of your identifier, the NRIC number in this case, or any other identifier that you use to access information and services that are not meant for them, they will do so.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It comes back to the fundamental point, even if you cannot work out the full identifier from a partial identifier, as long as that identifier is used for the purposes of authentication or as password, you still have a problem.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I hope that explains our position and our thinking.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Gerald Giam had a clarification on the difficulties encountered by users with respect to share transfer forms and annual returns on the new Bizfile portal.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Can I just confirm with Mr Giam that that has nothing to do with the NRIC numbers issue?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, firstly, extension given; second, no penalty; and third, if anyone is having difficulty with their filing still, please do contact ACRA and their service personnel will assist.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Was it done for the new Bizfile portal?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I do not have details on what kind of testing exactly was done, but what I think I can say with relative confidence is that some testing was done.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The question on this specific testing, I do not have the answer to that.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But anyway, anybody who is experiencing difficulty, please contact ACRA and they will assist you; and in the meantime, they are working to resolve any technical difficulties.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: It is useful to reiterate the distinction, as acknowledged by Minister Teo, between an individual acknowledging that the NRIC number is neither a foolproof nor secure method for personal identification and, hence, may be desensitised; and the same individual consenting and being comfortable with their NRIC being released or broadly disseminated.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Most Singaporeans will agree the former, but strongly disagree with the latter.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: My questions have to do with the implications of this distinction.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: For Minister Teo, going forward, would the Government's policy of desensitising the NRIC number also lead to difficulties in the practical implementation of low-grade access restrictions, such as passwords for PDF documents, like she mentioned early on, that contain confidential, but not secret information.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And relatedly, whether there have been any feasibility studies on what a widespread desensitised NRIC policy could mean for the day-to-day operation of businesses in our economy?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: For Minister Indranee, if indeed it was within the Government's rights to release personal information on company directors, according to the ACRA Act, could this, then, deter individuals from being willing to take up directorships, especially for small and micro businesses where friends and family are often roped in as directors?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And, if so, whether some kind of opt-out clause for deep, personal information, including address and NRIC number, beyond just the name, for directors for such small firms, would be possible?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Because at least for smaller firms, these kind of deep due diligence may not be necessary.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: First, I believe that his opening sentence in his preamble is erroneous.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We did not say that the NRIC number is not suitable for identification.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: You can use it to identify a person.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: You cannot use the NRIC number to prove that the person is who he claims to be.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I do appreciate that there is a lot to take on board, so, I would refer Assoc Prof Jamus Lim to the specific statements on this topic of drawing a distinction between the NRIC number as an identifier and as an authenticator, so that we could have a proper understanding of what it is.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The second response to his comments is that, I am not sure that it is useful to characterise what we are doing as desensitising.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As I explained, we are not making a change to allow the full NRIC number to be widely disclosed.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Nowhere in this description is there a need to refer to desensitisation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I am not sure that that characterisation applies to what we are seeking to do and I would encourage Members not to use this characterisation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The only change we are making is to stop incorrect uses of NRIC numbers as authenticators and as passwords.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim asked whether the ability to make known NRIC numbers might deter individuals from taking up directorships and whether there can be some kind of opt-out clause.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is necessary to go back to first principles and the very basics of corporate governance.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The reason why you have information available is for corporate transparency.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: You must protect the public because anybody who sets up a business and transacts with the public, interfaces with a member of the public; and that member of the public transacting with you, may run into difficulties or issues and must then know whom they are dealing with.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Let us take an example that people can relate to – say, your home renovation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Most times, it could be a company or, say, a sole proprietorship.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is Mr Wong trading as General Renovations and the name card will say "General Renovations".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: You have no idea who the company "General Renovations" is.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: You will go to Bizfile, you will search "General Renovations" and you will find that it is Mr Wong trading as General Renovations.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But there could be many other Mr Wongs as well.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Hence, it is about looking at it through a different lens.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If anybody has a concern that they do not wish to have their NRIC number known and, for that reason, do not become a corporate director, that perhaps may be a step too far.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But the bottom line is, in our regime, as well as in many other countries, if you are going to do business and transact with the public, the public has to know who you are and be able to contact you.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: To the extent that we can make some concessions, we have done so.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For example, under the last round of amendments, you can now put a separate contact address instead of your residential address.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, if somebody needed to sue you, they could leave the Writ of Summons at your office.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: They do not necessarily have to go to your residence.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, we have made some shifts, but on identification, there is no running away from the fact that you still need to be able to identify the individual you are dealing with.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Okay, we are approaching the end of time for the Ministerial Statements.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Leong, are you asking a clarification to the Minister's response, not a new clarification?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, can I ask the question again: whether the circular was cleared by any political office holders and whether political office holders were giving directions when civil servants in ACRA and MDDI were clarifying with one another on the instruction in the circular?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: That was not in your preamble, that was your question.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Leong had actually made a couple of statements.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I clarified that that was what he was saying and, far from taking credit, I thanked him for his position.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On the second question, I actually partially answered it, but I have checked.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Orders of the day.
